consensus_summary: Door/gate primarily means Christ as the exclusive access/entrance to salvation and God’s presence, with common secondary senses of ministry opportunity, the heart’s door, civic power/judgment, and eschatological inclusion or exclusion.
book_summary: Jesus is the destination of the Way and the threshold into the covenant house, its posts marked by blood and the word of God; heaven’s gates also mark the constellations through which the New Moon appears.
consensus_core_identification: Christ as the door/gate of access to salvation
book_core_identification: Jesus as threshold into the covenant house (destination of the Way)
boundary_disagreement: Book keeps the Christological door but adds covenant-house posts marked by blood and the word, and reassigns ‘heaven’s gates’ to celestial markers of the New Moon’s monthly path—cases and a referent layer absent from the consensus primary and alternatives.
rationale: Minimum cores both identify Jesus/Christ as the door/threshold of entrance into salvation or the covenant people, so the central referent is preserved and equivalent. Extra consensus detail (narrow gate, open door of opportunity, gates of Hades, etc.) and the book’s Passover/mezuzah and constellation elaborations do not replace that core; they alter extension. The astronomical New-Moon mapping and the explicit post-marking conditions therefore refine rather than match or overturn the consensus.
strongest_objection: Printed citations support Jesus as door, blood on posts, word on gates, Bethel as gate of heaven, and New Jerusalem gates, but give no warrant for the constellation/New Moon claim, which is pure addition.
